title: Parcel delivery SMS phishing wave
text: A smishing wave impersonating a national postal service asked recipients to pay a small customs fee. Text messages contained the short link http://track-parcel-delivery.test/p/8812. The landing page collected card numbers, expiry dates and one-time passwords. The domain track-parcel-delivery.test rotated hosting between 192.0.2.61 and 192.0.2.62. Messages were sent from foreign mobile numbers and the kit geo-fenced visitors so that crawlers outside the target country only saw a blank page.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Invoice lure with malicious HTML attachment
text: Finance departments were targeted with emails titled 'Overdue invoice - action required'. The attachment Invoice_8841.html opened a fake webmail login form rendered locally, which avoided URL reputation filters. Captured credentials were sent through a POST request to hxxp://invoice-docs-share[.]test/collect.php. The attachment had the MD5 a158d158545862a3f91096a1a1f8ec7e. Sender addresses spoofed a known supplier and the reply-to header pointed to a free mail service. Users who entered their password were later targeted by business email compromise attempts.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Postal smishing kit reused with new domains
text: The customs fee smishing kit reappeared with fresh domains. Messages now link to http://parcel-redelivery.test/r/119 while the older track-parcel-delivery.test redirects to the same panel. Collected card data is exfiltrated to a messaging bot. The hosting IP 192.0.2.62 is shared with the previous wave. The kit checks the user agent and only displays the form to mobile browsers.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: CV-themed phishing delivering a password stealer
text: Recruiters received emails from fake candidates with a ZIP archive named Resume_Julia.zip. The archive contained a shortcut file that downloaded a small password stealer from hxxp://cv-portfolio-host[.]example/files/resume.bin. The dominant activity is the phishing delivery; the payload (SHA-256 349a6e19a66a3730b6e5fd625a8ac4190fcd5a9344d4c14b1473991c784890c1) only collected browser passwords. The social-engineering pretext was carefully crafted around open job offers published on LinkedIn.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: LockMare ransomware delivered after payroll phishing
text: A transport company was hit by LockMare ransomware. Initial access came from the payroll phishing campaign, the employee's stolen credentials being reused on the VPN from 198.51.100.24. The operators used PowerShell to disable endpoint protection and deployed the locker (MD5 7ccb9f68bfa7dafa8368fcc001b21254) on every server. Files were renamed with the .lmare extension and the ransom note pointed to lockmare-pay.test. Encryption of the ERP database halted operations for four days.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: LockMare encryptor technical analysis
text: The LockMare encryptor uses a hybrid scheme: each file is encrypted with a random symmetric key which is then protected with the operator's public key. It skips system folders to keep the machine bootable, deletes shadow copies and empties the recycle bin. The sample analysed (MD5 7ccb9f68bfa7dafa8368fcc001b21254, SHA-256 edf3e44a602937862e5fc72fde2b6a58db791e109df146fbb8b7f1715d1a51c5) contains a hardcoded payment page http://lockmare-pay.test/victim/portal. No decryption flaw was identified.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Ransomware incident at a manufacturing plant
text: Production lines stopped after a ransomware attack encrypted the engineering workstations. The attackers stopped database and backup services before launching the encryption, then left a note named RESTORE-FILES.txt. Investigation found the binary svchosts.exe with MD5 71bb27e391dd8596ebbbf9ada0e56410. Network logs showed outbound traffic to restore-files-help.invalid and 198.51.100.230. The company restored from offline backups and did not pay.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: LockMare exfiltration tooling
text: Before deploying LockMare, the affiliates exfiltrate data with a renamed sync utility to 198.51.100.88. The extortion note claims the publication of stolen documents on lockmare-pay.test if no payment is received. Investigators recovered the locker with MD5 7ccb9f68bfa7dafa8368fcc001b21254 on three domain controllers. Victims are mainly logistics and transport companies.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Loader distributing multiple payloads via fake updates
text: Compromised websites display a fake browser update banner. The downloaded script launches an obfuscated PowerShell loader that fetches the next stage from hxxps://browser-update-cdn[.]test/u/stage2.dat. Depending on the victim profile, the loader installs a banking trojan or a remote access tool. The PowerShell script hash is ebf7321eba38c34007dae5fa278c340e77ec648fb7a6a61ec489deff9531ece3. The loader checks for sandbox artefacts before running.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Destructive wiper targeting energy companies
text: A wiper named Ashfall overwrote the master boot record and the first megabytes of every file on infected machines of an energy company. Unlike ransomware, no ransom was requested and recovery was impossible without backups. The wiper was deployed via group policy from a compromised domain controller. The sample has SHA-256 9e3069b9197098768f1e7ef7bb50649483ef76c74ede8a9d60b1f4d8a8721b21 and contacted 203.0.113.33 to report completion.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Fake update loader infrastructure
text: The fake browser update loader rotated its infrastructure. The second stage is now hosted at browser-update-cdn.test and browser-patch-cdn.test, with the same payload delivery logic. Captured payloads include a remote access tool with SHA-256 1e3d8ce642cbd253a214eb31c1c5ac46d1d9f02aab158e23054575d5825146be. Website owners should check their content management systems for injected scripts.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Malvertising campaign delivering remote access tool
text: Search engine advertisements for popular software led users to fake download pages at get-software-free.test. The installer bundled a legitimate program with a remote access tool (MD5 69d43553b0711cd27bbb77c978770ef3) which connects to 203.0.113.71. The operators use the access to deploy additional malware selectively.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Remote code execution in OrbitCMS through deserialization
text: A deserialization flaw in OrbitCMS (CVE-2099-0311) allows unauthenticated remote code execution by sending a serialized object in a cookie. Proof-of-concept code was published and exploitation started within 24 hours. Exploited servers downloaded a script from http://orbit-cms-patch.example/fix.sh, which installed a backdoor. Scanning activity originated from 203.0.113.12 and 203.0.113.13.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: OrbitCMS exploitation leads to web shell deployment
text: Incident responders observed the exploitation of the OrbitCMS deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2099-0311) on a media company website. The attacker deployed a PHP web shell at https://www.media-site.test/uploads/thumb.php and used it to read the database configuration. The exploitation requests came from 203.0.113.12, already seen in mass scanning.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Exchange-like mail server exploitation chain
text: An exploitation chain targeting on-premises mail servers combines a server-side request forgery (CVE-2099-1101) and a post-authentication code execution (CVE-2099-1102). Attackers drop web shells in the web root and use them to export mailboxes. The web shell MD5 is 697791d8808a4f1831593f34e6737951. Exploitation sources included 198.51.100.33.
notes: Synthetic report written for the academic prototype; indicators are fictitious (RFC 5737 / RFC 2606 / RFC 6761).

title: Exploitation of a JavaScript framework prototype pollution
text: A prototype pollution issue in a server-side JavaScript framework (CVE-2099-1333) can lead to remote code execution. Exploitation attempts targeted e-commerce websites and came from 203.0.113.120. The payload attempted to download a script from http://node-pkg-cache.test/p.js. Developers should upgrade the dependency and validate JSON input.
